introduction: Follow Venmar’s exact scalp exchange and explore the separate dragon, forest, prisoner, village and Meopham stories.
orientation: Explore the forest and Lylrstas, meet Venmar the dragon and follow his request. Actual arrival discovers this zone; meeting Venmar reveals his exchange.
Ask Venmar about evil or ogre. These two aliases share one response about his summoning and the ogre in the woods.

Venmar accepts one exact ogre scalp for the drow skin boots. BBryt carries that scalp in the hollow tree; the native source is carried stock rather than a carving result. An exact supplied scalp also fits. The recipe does not require a remembered personal kill, greeting, first-source recovery or prison rescue.

The scalp is authored as hidden and cannot be sold, located or rented. Recovering and offering it require their actual visibility and custody admission; the optional material row only shows current loose inventory.
Offer the exact scalp loose to Venmar. Accepted history is separate from current material and reward possession. Spent materials or missing boots do not erase the recorded exchange.
Venmar departs after the native exchange. A departure message, a missing dragon or his reset declaration cannot substitute for accepted reward and retirement outcomes.
The tree entrance resets hidden and closed. Its platform has a chance of falling during command dispatch; locating an entrance, opening it, crossing it and surviving a fall are different events.

The forest and Lylrstas form one local route, while Meopham has a separate approach. The selected surface rooms lack reciprocal entry exits in the static source; builders must qualify actual arrival before advertising a usable approach.
The prison contains five distinct captives. Finding the guard’s key or opening a cell does not prove release from restraints, consent, a surviving escort or lasting freedom.
One prison door has different keys on its two sides. The vault chest has an unsupported trap damage type. Both need played diagnosis and a balanced builder repair plan.
Cionvra and the Lylrstas barkeep have native supply shops. Native purchases currently refuse while accounting is active; supplied items and acknowledged purchases are separate facts.

Both barkeeps can dispatch generated world quests. Those paid assignments, maps, returns and rewards belong to the world-quest system rather than Venmar’s scalp exchange. Hylga has no local drink shop declaration.

Sakthris redirects coin-exchange requests to the Royal Bank. The counter’s sign advertises banking commands, while its assigned interaction is locker entry. Actual banking and locker outcomes need their own admitted callers.
The Lylrstas inn has an explicitly assigned rent handler, despite lacking the raw inn flag. Inn wording, light or a room visit does not prove safe storage, healing or protection.
The cyan potion is configured for armor, serious vigor and barkskin; the vault staff is configured for earthquake. Custody, charges, admitted use and actual beneficiary effects are separate outcomes.

The summoned dragon, captives, village families, guards, animals, town cleaners, library and bar suggest wider stories. Builders must define real contributions, choices, beneficiaries and lasting results. New tracking requires active READY accounting. Daily replay remains disabled until source availability, exact exchange, giver retirement, reward/save/replay and accountable renewal are qualified.
